editorial.headline: The Transport Work That Happens Between the Journeys
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the organising, planning and in-transit handling work that keeps transport, storage and distribution operations moving.
editorial.body:
Transport is often understood through the visible journey: the train, road vehicle, vessel or aircraft in motion. This activity concerns much of the work around that journey instead. It covers arranging or organising transport operations across rail, road, sea and air, alongside logistics consultancy for transport, warehousing and distribution operations. Its scope also reaches the management of logistics for sports equipment and supplies, as well as practical cargo-handling work during transit.

That last distinction matters. The handling included here is specifically tied to moving goods: temporary protective packing while goods are in transit, unpacking, sampling and weighing. Taken together, the scope describes a broad operational layer of transport support—where planning, coordination and controlled handling meet. It is an activity for businesses whose role is to make transport and distribution systems function coherently, whether through advisory work, operational organisation or carefully bounded goods handling.

Registration is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The national position is TERBUKA to foreign investment, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. At the national level, the record therefore permits full foreign ownership. That position is grounded in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For founders, the important point is not to confuse a broad activity title with a narrow operational remit: the business description should remain anchored to transport-support operations, logistics consultancy and the specified transit-related handling tasks.

Bali does not place this activity within its island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium for Low and Medium-Low risk activities. The Bali record places it at medium-high risk and says it is not blocked by that moratorium. This is therefore not a case where a foreign investor is nationally open yet unable to register in Bali today. Still, the record calls for verification by address. That is the honest Bali position: no moratorium block is identified for this activity, but the proposed location should be checked before treating the national 100% ceiling as a completed Bali registration outcome.
